main_text.p: ad martyria fese prodere non debe- rent, captis tamen non licebat manu armata resistere ; sed armis, & virtute patientiæ,quæcunque tormentorum immania genera superare, quo admi- rabilior reluceret virtus Crucis Christi. Quod autem populo Christiano non deesset ad sui defensionem vi- res & potestas, insinuat alibi: ] vbi dirigimur ad illum per insignem locum, in fine Exhortationis ad Demetrianum Africæ Præsidem ; [lædere servos Dei & Christi, persequutionibus tuis de- sine,quos læsos ultio divina defendit. Inde est enim, quòd nemo nostrum quando apprehenditur, reluctatur; nec se adversus injustam violentiam vestram, quamuis nimius & copiosus populus noster ulciscitur. ] Et cùm jam Imperatoris Edicto, ad extremum supplicium postularetur, martyrijque quasi candidatus esset : Presbyteris, Diaconis, & universæ plebi Carthagi-nensi per {f}Epistolâ huiusmodi orationem habuit; [Vos autem Fratres charissimi,) pro disciplina quam de mandatis dominicis à me semper accepistisf Lib.9. epist.1. edit. Rom.

page.notes: The marginal note reads "Lib.9." with a doubtful "9" (could be a 4); marked [?] in the note. Ornamental "„" marks at the ends of lines are printed line-fillers and are not transcribed. Brackets "[", "]" and ")" are printed as they stand. The text ends on the half-line "piftis", which is completed as "accepistis" on the same line; the final word is continued from the line above by hyphenation. No catchword, signature or other printed furniture is visible at the foot of the page.
